00050 #define DEFAULT_UGEN_DOCS <I>Not yet documented although the argument name should be reasonably clear</I>.
00051 #define COMMON_UGEN_DOCS  <B>Generic %UGen argument documentation:</B>                    \
00052               Arguments which are UGen type can be continuously controlled and these        \
00053               may generally be multichannel (although there are some exceptions).         \
00054               Arguments which are constant/literal values (e.g., float or int) are clearly    \
00055               not continuously controllable and not multichannel (therefore will          \
00056               generallly be applied identically to each channel should the UGen being       \
00057               created is made multichannel via other arguments.                 \
00058               Arguments which are Buffer type may require a Buffer for some specific        \
00059               purpose (e.g, TableOsc uses a buffer for its wavetable) but single channel      \
00060               Buffer objects are also used to specify an array of literal values (e.g., LLine)  \
00061               \n\
00062               \n\

01421 #define EVENT_COMMON_UGEN_DOCS  <B>Generic Event-based %UGen argument documentation:</B>                    \
01422                 Event-based UGen instances are created using a template where the first template parameter    \
01423                 is an "event" class (i.e., a subclass of EventBase<OwnerType>) and the second template      \
01424                 parameter is an "owner" type. This must be the same owner type as the event.          \
01425                 Generally a event UGen will be constructed in one of two ways: using a pointer to the     \
01426                 owner which will be used to construct an event of the appropriate type (in turn passing     \
01427                 the owner pointer); or the event UGen may be constructed by passing in an existing        \
01428                 event. This is useful if the event is complex and/or has a custom constructor and       \
01429                 the default constructor(s) are therfore insufficient. Using this method be sure that your   \
01430                 event class can be safely copied (e.g., using normal copy constructors) so don`t store      \
01431                 regular pointers owned by the event class. UGen++ ojects such as Buffer and UGen are fine   \
01432                 since these enclose reference-counted objects.                          \
01433                 \n\n\
01434                 COMMON_UGEN_DOCS
